content: Primidone is a medication prescribed to control seizures. It may also be used for other purposes, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Primidone is available in tablet and liquid suspension forms, taken orally. Initially, it is usually taken once daily at bedtime, with the dosage gradually increased to three or four times a day. It can be taken with food. If using the suspension, shake it well before each use. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take primidone exactly as directed. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not take it more frequently than instructed. This medication must be taken regularly to be effective. Do not skip doses, even if you feel you do not need them. Do not stop taking primidone without consulting your doctor, as abrupt discontinuation can cause seizures. Your doctor will likely reduce your dose gradually if discontinuation is necessary. Primidone is also used to treat tremors. Discuss the potential risks of using this medication for your condition with your doctor. Before taking primidone, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to primidone or any other drugs. Also, let them know if you have had adverse reactions to barbiturates such as amobarbital, butabarbital, pentobarbital, phenobarbital, or secobarbital. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially acetazolamide, anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), antihistamines, carbamazepine, disulfiram, doxycycline, griseofulvin, isoniazid, MAO inhibitors, medications for depression, seizures, pain, asthma, colds, or allergies, muscle relaxants, nicotinamide, oral contraceptives, phenytoin, sedatives, sleeping pills, steroids, tranquilizers, valproic acid, and vitamins. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had anemia, or lung, kidney, or liver disease. Use a non-oral method of birth control while taking primidone, as it can reduce the effectiveness of oral contraceptives. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking primidone, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking primidone. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can increase the drowsiness caused by this drug. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Mild side effects of primidone may include drowsiness, incoordination, irritability, excitement (in children), upset stomach, tiredness, headache, and changes in appetite. Contact your doctor if these symptoms are severe or persistent. Other possible side effects include restlessness, hair loss, swollen eyelids or legs, double vision, blurred vision, and changes in sexual drive or ability. Severe side effects require immediate medical attention. These include seizures, sore throat, fever, severe skin rash, yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, bloody nose, unusual bleeding, tiny purple skin spots, and easy bruising. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store primidone in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Do not freeze the suspension. Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as certain tests will be ordered to monitor your response to primidone. Your dose may need frequent adjustments, especially when starting the medication. Effectiveness may vary between different brands of primidone, so do not switch brands without consulting your pharmacist. Contact your doctor if you continue to experience seizures. Carry identification (e.g., Medic Alert) stating that you have epilepsy and are taking primidone. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
